title: Canary Regression Radar: lightweight divergence detector and preflight scoring for rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current preflight suites focus on binary pass/fail smoke tests and heavy perf evals. We lack a lightweight, continuous canary-level signal that detects subtle behavioral drift (quality regressions) and correlated token-level perf anomalies before they affect production traffic. This ticket introduces the 'Regression Radar': a compact canary divergence detector and scoring layer that runs as part of preflight and canary pipelines to provide an early, explainable hit/miss signal for rollouts and LTS promotions.

Goals: 1) Produce a deterministic divergence score per canary batch that combines semantic and token-level metrics (KL divergence over next-token distributions, top-k overlap, and eval task accuracy). 2) Surface a single canonical 'radar score' with heatmap-backed explanations per prompt group to the Console and runbooks. 3) Make the detector lightweight (sub-200ms per sample) so it can run in preflight and quick canary checks without adding large cost. 4) Integrate with rollout gates to automatically mark canary as FAIL/WARN/OK based on thresholds and to feed rollback automation.

Scope: - Implementation of divergence scoring service and library (Python/Go) to be used by preflight runner. - Small seed prompt set and partitioning by workload (short chat, long context, embeddings consistency). - Integration points: preflight runner, canary orchestration, Console dashboard alerts, runbook hooks. - Tests: unit, integration with smoke battery, simulated production traces for false positive rate assessment.

Out of scope: extensive large-scale perf evals, new model benchmarks, changing rollout policies themselves (will add hooks only).
acceptance_criteria: Radar library produces a deterministic numeric 'radar_score' for a given canary batch (0-100, lower is better)
Three explanation channels available per sample: token-KL heatmap, top-k overlap, per-prompt evaluation result (pass/fail) and aggregated summary
Integration with preflight runner so that every canary run emits radar_score + artifacts to the Console and to the release orchestration API
Defined FAIL/WARN/OK thresholds documented and test fixtures that assert expected transitions
End-to-end tests demonstrate false-positive rate < 3% on historical upgrade traces and detection rate > 90% for injected regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for divergence computations (KL, top-k overlap, token entropy)
Micro-benchmarks to ensure per-sample overhead < 200ms on our canary hardware
Integration test that runs radar against a held-out set of historical canary traces and confirms scoring stability
Attack tests: inject a controlled quality regression and validate radar_score crosses the FAIL threshold
Canary run in dedicated sandbox with Console wiring and alert firing to oncall channel
rollout_gates: Hard FAIL: radar_score >= 70 (immediate canary halt and automatic rollback)
Warn: radar_score between 50 and 70 (requires human approval in Console before progressing)
OK: radar_score < 50 (allow automated continuation to next stage)
LTS promotion: stricter thresholds (FAIL >= 60) and mandatory manual review step
metrics: token-KL mean and 95th percentile per prompt group
top-k overlap rate and per-prompt delta vs baseline
end-to-end detection latency (time from canary start to emitted radar_score)
false-positive / false-negative measured against historical labeled regressions
runbook: If radar_score >= 70: abort rollout, run rollback playbook (link below), notify oncall, capture full sample artifacts and perf traces
If radar_score 50-70: open a canary review in Console, attach radar artifacts and recommended suspect prompts, optionally run targeted evals
If radar_score < 50: continue automated rollout but schedule follow-up stability checks at 1h and 24h intervals
For LTS promotions: require runbook signoff with checklist: perf regression pass, radar artifacts reviewed, QA acceptance
implementation_notes: Scoring components: token-KL computed on normalized logits (temperature-corrected), top-k Jaccard overlap on model top-20 preds, and small task-eval harness for critical prompts
Use a small, fixed prompt seed (20-40 prompts) partitioned by workload to keep cost low; prompts stored in versioned asset bucket
Cache warmup probe: run KV prefix warmup prior to scoring to avoid cold-cache bias in token distributions
Statistical smoothing: use EWMA across consecutive canary batches to reduce noise and prevent oscillation-triggered rollbacks
Expose a 'why' artifact bundle: per-sample heatmaps, diffs vs baseline logits, and a plain-language summary for Console
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy signals cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, EWMA smoothing, human-in-the-loop for WARN band
Risk: performance overhead on preflight. Mitigation: micro-benchmarks and hard perf budget; sample set size adjustable by config
Risk: gaming by model changes that alter token distributions without quality loss. Mitigation: combine semantic evals with token metrics and surface explanations for triage
Risk: storage of logits/artifacts increases cost and PII risk. Mitigation: limit retention, redact samples, and encrypt artifacts at rest
